title: fix: restore README star history chart with committed snapshot
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- The star-history.com embed currently renders a "GitHub restricted access to star data" placeholder (GitHub stargazer API restriction), so the README chart has been broken.
- Replaces the remote embed with committed light/dark SVG snapshots generated from the repo's own stargazer data (4,947 stars as of 2026-08-14).
- Adds `.github/scripts/star-history-chart.mjs` to generate the snapshots; output is deterministic, so unchanged star data produces identical files.
- The daily README workflow (`docs-update-readme-news.yml`) now regenerates the charts with the bot token and commits them alongside the news update; the chart step is `continue-on-error` so a stargazer API failure can't block the news refresh.
- The chart still links to star-history.com; the live embed can be restored once the restriction lifts.
- Supersedes #13315, which pointed the chart at a third-party mirror (closed — part of a cross-repo campaign).

Note for after merge: trigger `Docs / Update README` via workflow_dispatch once to confirm the bot app token can read stargazer data (all local testing used a personal collaborator token).

gist.headline: The stars return home
gist.blurb: The README's star chart was replaced by a rather unhelpful GitHub restriction notice. It now grows from a committed snapshot of the hive's own stargazer data instead.
gist.summary: Replaced the broken remote star-history.com README embed with deterministic committed light and dark SVG charts generated from Pollinations' stargazer data, currently showing 4,947 stars.
gist.impact: README visitors can once again see the project's star history, while the daily docs workflow refreshes the chart alongside news updates without letting a stargazer API hiccup block the refresh.
